data.claim: gate run and review already tick; ci run and the post-merge check do not
data.falsifier: an item ci run renews lease.renewed events
data.mechanism: CI.run called CommandRunner with no on_tick
data.probe_output: 3 failed, 2 passed (ci tests fail, gate and review tick tests pass)
data.question: Which long operations fail to renew the caller's lease?

evidence.note: research note added; 3 of 5 new tests fail on unfixed code
ddflow brief read; decisions D-company-workflows (knob [lease].renew_long_commands covers it), r-reuse-core (LK.keeper/throttled reused)
CI.run takes tick; api.ci.lease_tick wired in cirun.run and check_after_merge; tests/test_long_op_renew.py

chunk_findings.detail: These two tests only assert that an explicitly injected callback fires (`on_tick=lambda: seen.append(1)`), and they run against `tmp_path`/a bare `Reviewer` with no repo, no `init`, no `claim`, and no lease at all. Nothing in them can observe a `lease.renewed` event, so they pass even if the production `ddflow gate run` / `ddflow review` paths never wire a lease-bound tick into `run_command_gate`/`review` — i.e. even in the exact regression the change is meant to fix (an agent whose lease lapses during a 7-minute review). The module docstring promises "Every long operation renews the caller's lease … a gate command, a review's wait, and the CI run", but only `test_an_item_ci_run_renews_the_holders_lease` (via `_renewals`) actually checks a renewal; the gate and review claims are unverified. Only the CI path would catch a regression here.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_long_op_renew.py::test_a_command_gate_ticks_while_it_runs / test_a_review_waiting_on_a_slow_reviewer_ticks

chunk_findings.detail: The assertions are wall-clock-tight: each command sleeps 2.4 s while the tick interval is 1 s, and each requires `len(seen) >= 2`. Unless the implementation happens to tick immediately at t=0, the second tick lands on the boundary (t≈2.0 of a 2.4 s window, ~0.4 s of slack). These tests are collected under xdist (several disable `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER`), so on a loaded/oversubscribed runner a single 1 s sleep routinely overshoots and only one tick is observed, failing a correct implementation. Given the change is explicitly about long, slow operations, the margin should be several multiples of the interval (or the count should be derived from elapsed time), not 1.4×.

The whole point of this change is that the *production* `ddflow gate run` / `ddflow review` paths must renew the caller's lease (the new `lease_tick(...)` passed to `CI.run` in `cirun.py:97` is exactly that wiring). chunk_findings.detail: The review path — the case the intent names explicitly ("7+ minutes on the slow reviewer") — is still never exercised end-to-end through the `ddflow review` command, so the original regression can still pass this suite. `test_a_review_ticker_renews_the_holders_lease` calls `API_RV._lease_ticker(...)` in isolation and only proves the helper renews when handed a holder's `item`; it never shows that the `ddflow review` handler obtains that ticker and passes it in. `test_a_review_waiting_on_a_slow_reviewer_ticks` builds a bare `RV.Reviewer` and injects `on_tick=lambda: seen.append(1)`, so it only asserts that an explicitly supplied callback fires; it observes no `lease.renewed` event and does not go through `run_cli`. If the production wiring in the review CLI were reverted to `on_tick=None` (the exact bug), both tests would still pass: the first because it calls the helper directly, the second because the fake lambda is supplied by the test itself. Contrast the gate (`test_a_gate_run_renews_the_holders_lease`, which runs `run_cli(repo, "gate", "run", ...)` against a claimed lease and asserts `_renewals(repo) > before`) and CI (`test_an_item_ci_run_renews_the_holders_lease` via `cirun.run`), which do cover their CLI wiring. So previous finding 1 is answered for gate/CI but still holds for review: the new helper test does not answer it because nothing ties `_lease_ticker` to the `ddflow review` entry point.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_long_op_renew.py::test_a_review_ticker_renews_the_holders_lease / test_a_review_waiting_on_a_slow_reviewer_ticks

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds. The production side of this diff wires the renewal in exactly the two places the tests are supposed to protect — `ddflow/api/ci.py` (`tick=lease_tick(log, cfg, st, item)` on the `CI.run(...)` call) and `ddflow/api/cirun.py` (`tick=lease_tick(log, cfg, st, item)`) — but the tests still inject `on_tick=lambda: seen.append(1)` against `tmp_path` / a bare `Reviewer` with no repo, no `init`, no `claim` and no lease, and assert only that their own callback fired. Concrete demonstration: delete `tick=lease_tick(log, cfg, st, item)` from the `CI.run` call in `ddflow/api/cirun.py`, or make `lease_tick` in `ddflow/api/ci.py` return `None` unconditionally, and both tests stay green even though the exact regression they exist for (an agent's lease lapsing while `gate run` / `review` blocks) is fully reintroduced. The tests can never observe a `lease.renewed` event, so they do not answer this finding.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_long_op_renew.py::test_a_command_gate_ticks_while_it_runs / test_a_review_waiting_on_a_slow_reviewer_ticks

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds. The new helper fixes the tick interval at the value the tests already depend on: `every = float(max(1, cfg.lease.heartbeat_s))` in `ddflow/api/ci.py` clamps the interval to 1 s, while each test sleeps ~2.4 s and requires `len(seen) >= 2`. Unless a tick fires at t=0, the second tick lands at t≈2.0 s of a 2.4 s window (~0.4 s of slack). These tests are collected under xdist (several force a worker name), so on an oversubscribed runner one 1 s sleep routinely overshoots and a correct implementation observes only one tick, failing. Nothing in this diff widens that margin or makes the assertion event-count-based on lease state instead of wall clock.

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds. Nothing in this diff adds an end-to-end assertion that `ddflow gate run` / `ddflow review` actually pass a *lease-bound* tick into `run_command_gate`/`review`. The ci.py change only shows that `run_ci` accepts and forwards a `tick` tuple; it does not demonstrate that the production callers supply `(lease.renew, n)` rather than a no-op or nothing. The tests in question still exercise an explicitly injected `on_tick=lambda: seen.append(1)` against `tmp_path`/a bare `Reviewer` with no repo, no `init`, no `claim`, and no lease, so they pass even in the exact regression this change targets — an agent whose lease lapses because the production path never wires a lease-bound tick. The fix (a plumbed `tick` parameter) is necessary but not sufficient, and no probe here observes a `lease.renewed` event.

chunk_findings.title: tests/test_long_op_renew.py::test_a_ci_run_ticks_while_the_command_runs / test_a_command_gate_ticks_while_it_runs / test_a_review_waiting_on_a_slow_reviewer_ticks

chunk_findings.detail: This file was added to answer the earlier finding 1 — that `test_a_command_gate_ticks_while_it_runs` and `test_a_review_waiting_on_a_slow_reviewer_ticks` only assert an injected callback fires and can never observe a `lease.renewed` event. For the *gate* path that is now genuinely covered: `test_a_gate_run_renews_the_holders_lease` drives `ddflow gate run` through `run_cli` and its gate command exits only once a `lease.renewed` line exists, so removing the gate's lease-bound tick makes `assert _renewals(repo) > before` fail. For the *review* path the finding still holds. `test_a_review_ticker_renews_the_holders_lease` does not exercise `review` or the `ddflow review` CLI at all; it constructs the ticker itself with `tick = API_RV._lease_ticker(log, cfg, st.items["T1"], 0.2)`, sleeps, calls `tick()` and counts events. That only pins down that the `_lease_ticker` helper renews and logs. `test_a_review_waiting_on_a_slow_reviewer_ticks` is unchanged in kind: it passes `on_tick=lambda: seen.append(1)`, a raw lambda that touches no lease. So the exact regression the change exists to prevent — `ddflow review` (or `RV.review`'s production default) never being handed a lease-bound keeper, let alone being handed `None` — is not detected by this file; deleting the wiring that passes `_lease_ticker`'s result into `review`/the CLI leaves every assertion green. A test that ran `ddflow review --agent me` against a slow reviewer (or that asserted `review(...)` without an explicit `on_tick` still renews the holder's lease) would be needed to close finding 1 for review. The docstring's claim ("The wiring of `ddflow review`: its tick is the holder's throttled keeper") overstates what the body verifies.

Under xdist or a loaded/oversubscribed runner a single 1 s sleep routinely overshoots, so a correct implementation that ticks only once can fail these tests — a flaky test, and the triage is untriaged.

chunk_findings.detail: The review path — the case the intent names explicitly ("7+ minutes on the slow reviewer") — is still never exercised end-to-end through the `ddflow review` command, so the original regression can still pass this suite. `test_a_review_ticker_renews_the_holders_lease` calls `API_RV._lease_ticker(...)` in isolation and only proves the helper renews when handed a holder's `item`; it never shows that the `ddflow review` handler obtains that ticker and passes it in. `test_a_review_waiting_on_a_slow_reviewer_ticks` builds a bare `RV.Reviewer` and injects `on_tick=lambda: seen.append(1)`, so it only asserts that an explicitly supplied callback fires; it observes no `lease.renewed` event and does not go through `run_cli`. If the production wiring in the review CLI were reverted to `on_tick=None` (the exact bug), both tests would still pass: the first because it calls the helper directly, the second because the fake lambda is supplied by the test itself. Contrast the gate (`test_a_gate_run_renews_the_holders_lease`, which runs `run_cli(repo, "gate", "run", ...)` against a claimed lease and asserts `_renewals(repo) > before`) and CI (`test_an_item_ci_run_renews_the_holders_lease` via `cirun.run`), which do cover their CLI wiring. So previous finding 1 is answered for gate/CI but still holds for review: the new helper test does not answer it because nothing ties `_lease_ticker` to the `ddflow review` entry point.

chunk_findings.detail: `git diff --name-only` prints paths verbatim, and `str.split()` breaks on any whitespace inside a path (a space is *not* one of the characters git quotes). The motivating case in the intent is a conflict in `README.md` plus a "setup transcript json" file; if that file's real name contains a space (e.g. `docs/setup transcript.json`), git prints it as one line, `r.out.split()` turns it into the two tokens `docs/setup` and `transcript.json`, and the new message reports two non-existent conflicting files. The same broken token also fails the `f in pinned` membership test, so for exactly the files this change was written to explain, the "is a pin file / run `ddflow pins regenerate`" branch silently never fires. The same line is also wrong for git's quoted output (`core.quotePath` C-quotes non-ASCII names, e.g. `"pins/\303\251.json"`), which will never match a `pathlib`-produced entry from `pin_files`. The correct form is to parse NUL-delimited output plus `-z` (or `core.quotePath=false` and a line split), not whitespace splitting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci_conflict.py:17 (`conflicting_files`, `r.out.split()`)

chunk_findings.detail: The mixed-conflict test is named for separation ("separates pin files from the rest") and mirrors the reported incident (a pin file plus an ordinary file both conflicting), but its assertions only check the positive side: `"README.md is a pin file" in res.reason` and `"resolve notes.txt" in res.reason`. It never asserts that `notes.txt` is *not* reported as a pin file, and it does not bound the number of files blamed on the pin remedy. A plausible implementation bug — e.g. once any conflicting file is a pin file, the pin-remedy block lists *all* conflicting files (or marks the whole conflict as pin-related) — still satisfies all three tests: test 1 passes (README.md is both declared and conflicting), test 2 passes because no pin file conflicts there so the block is suppressed, and test 3 passes because both substrings are present even when notes.txt is spuriously labelled a pin file. Given the real trigger was README.md (pin) + setup transcript JSON (non-pin) conflicting together, this is exactly the case that should assert `"notes.txt is a pin file" not in res.reason` (or that the pin group is `== ["README.md"]`).

chunk_findings.detail: The pin-file branch of `cause()` tells the user to resolve a pin-file conflict either by running `ddflow pins regenerate` or by setting `[pins].after_merge` "so the post-merge hook does" (and the module docstring repeats the claim: "which the post-merge hook runs under `[pins].after_merge`"). But this text is produced *only* on the conflicted-merge path (`merge_tree`'s `if not m.ok:` branch), and a post-merge hook is run by `git merge` only when the merge completes without conflicts. With a conflicted merge, git stops before committing and runs no `post-merge`; completing the merge by hand with `git commit` runs `post-commit`, not `post-merge`. Concretely: branch has `README.md` (a pin file), main regenerated it, the CI scratch merge conflicts; the user follows the advice, sets `[pins].after_merge`, and runs `git merge main`/`ddflow merge` — the pin file conflicts again, the merge never completes, the hook never fires, and the pins stay stale. The automation advertised as an alternative remedy can therefore never trigger for the very failure it is printed for; the user must always regenerate by hand (or the automation would have to be wired to a conflict-time/pre-commit path, not a merge-completion hook).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci_conflict.py:29-35 (`cause`, the `[pins].after_merge` / "post-merge hook" remedy)
